answer: Computational proof-of-work resists Sybil attacks by requiring each agent to solve unique cryptographic puzzles. An attacker flooding the network faces a vast ocean of energy costs, as every identity demands dedicated CPU cycles. Like a fading ember, any node failing to provide sustained work loses its harbor in the consensus. This mechanism ensures that the cost of scaling an attack scales linearly with hardware requirements, making identity duplication technically and financially unfeasible for malicious actors.
